title: Appendix D — Four Master Tropes
role: Fourth Appendix essay and dissertation-portable in its own right. Burke develops metaphor / metonymy / synecdoche / irony not as figures of speech but as the four master tropes for the discovery and description of 'the truth'. He proposes the literal-realistic substitutions metaphor=perspective, metonymy=reduction, synecdoche=representation, irony=dialectic — and shows that each trope shades into the others (any one trope, fully developed, generates the other three). The essay is structured in five unlabeled roman-numeral sections corresponding to the four tropes plus a synthesizing fifth section. The trope-apparatus is parallel to but distinct from the pentad: tropes are the dialectical-rhetorical operations the pentad terms undergo. Generates a standalone Phase 3 synthesis deliverable (gm-four-master-tropes-manual) and cross-cuts every pentad-term entry in the Pentad Operationalization Manual.
